original_metadata.title: For closed oriented three-manifolds with a fixed distinguished two-tetrahedron framed-knot chain and nondegenerate Euclidean geometrization, acyclicity and normalized geometric torsion are preserved by relative triangulation changes
original_metadata.author: Jérôme Dubois; Igor G. Korepanov; Evgeniy V. Martyushev
original_metadata.source_title: A Euclidean Geometric Invariant of Framed (Un)Knots in Manifolds
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The construction must match infinitesimal vertex, edge-length, deficit-angle and rotation maps into a symmetric acyclic complex, rather than apply torsion to a given cellular complex. The author proves the relative Pachner connectivity and tracks the changing maximal minors through both the two-to-three and one-to-four moves. Exact edge-length and oriented-volume factors cancel against the normalization, while the same nonvanishing minors preserve acyclicity.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Read full relative Pachner connectivity Theorem1 on4-6, geometrization and signed deficit-angle setup7, infinitesimal rotation closure Lemma1 on7-8, all local derivative formulas and derivations9-10, complete based-complex definitions11-13, and full Theorem4 determinant and torsion comparison14-15. Select Theorem4 only: a closed oriented three-manifold with the same distinguished two-tetrahedron chain as Figures1/2, a consistently oriented nondegenerate Euclidean geometrization and initially acyclic complex(15). Relative Pachner moves avoid the distinguished chain; the authored minor changes preserve acyclicity and invariant(22). Standard stellar equivalence (Lickorish Theorem4.5) and based Reidemeister torsion are published foundations, and the local relative connectivity and geometric move cores are supplied here. No unconditional acyclicity assertion, knot detection theorem, independence from distinguished-tetrahedron geometry, or computed lens-space/framing examples selected. Exact selected statement and terminal proof pages rendered and visually inspected; physical headers/native ZIP members and source/license hashes checked. No independent mathematical reproof.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem4 with Convention1 triangulations of a closed oriented three-manifold, the same distinguished two-tetrahedron chain ABCD encoding the source framing, consistent orientations and vertex coordinates giving nonzero volume to every tetrahedron. Assume complex(15) is acyclic for the initial triangulation. Under relative Pachner triangulation changes preserving that chain, the resulting complex is acyclic and normalized geometric torsion I(M) in(22) is unchanged. Distinguished-chain geometry is fixed; no assertion that all such complexes are acyclic or that I separates knots.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The source assumes acyclicity in Convention3 and explicitly leaves a general acyclicity criterion unavailable. The selected title and scope retain this essential assumption. Remark13 allows dependence on distinguished-tetrahedron geometry; example independence is not generalized.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The complete original Theorem4 is retained with the fixed distinguished two-tetrahedron chain, nonzero geometric volumes and initial acyclicity. Relative Pachner connectivity, infinitesimal rotation/deficit maps, the symmetric chain complex, torsion convention, normalized invariant and full two-to-three/one-to-four minor calculation are bundled. Standard Reidemeister torsion and previously cited geometric identities remain foundations. No general acyclicity criterion, knot-separation property or distinguished-chain geometry independence is selected.
